conflicts.permit: Even if you delete Information, we may retain your Information in conformance with our data retention policy most specifically for legal and tax reasons and to honour your opt-out requests
conflicts.prohibit: We will delete all data and Information connected to your use of our Services.
conflicts.situation: A user who opted out of marketing asks, via the contact form, to delete the account and all stored data.
conflicts.reason: The deletion section promises deletion of all data except what law and tax reasons require. The contact section also allows retention to honour opt-out requests, and the policy does not say which governs.

conflicts.permit: We will report any such breach to the relevant law enforcement authorities and will co-operate with those authorities by disclosing your identity to them.
conflicts.prohibit: We will only share personal data in accordance with our Privacy Policy or if required to do so by a competent authority or court within the United Kingdom.
conflicts.situation: A user attempts unauthorised access to the Website, and the Premier League voluntarily discloses the user's identity to law enforcement without a UK court or authority requiring it.
conflicts.reason: The account clause limits sharing to the separate Privacy Policy or UK legal compulsion. The breach clause promises voluntary identity disclosure, and the Privacy Policy is not included to show whether it permits this.

conflicts.permit: Community Brands may access Customer Data for the purposes of providing and enhancing a service, preventing or addressing service or technical problems, responding to support issues, and responding to a Customer’s instructions, or as may be required by law, in accordance with the relevant Agreement between the Customer and Community Brands.
conflicts.prohibit: Community Brands will not access your Product Data or Services Data except in the following limited circumstances
conflicts.situation: Community Brands, on its own initiative and without a customer request, accesses data a customer entered while using its services to prevent a technical problem or enhance the service.
conflicts.reason: Customer Data appears to include Services Data. The limited circumstances allow support access only at the customer's request and omit service enhancement, and the policy does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may disclose your data to a third party if (i) we believe that disclosure is reasonably necessary to comply with any applicable law, regulation, legal process or government request (including to meet national security or law enforcement requirements), (ii) to enforce our agreements and policies
conflicts.prohibit: Community Brands will not provide your Product Data or Services Data to any third-party or permit any third-party to access your Product Data or Services Data, except with your permission or to comply with valid legal requirements such as a law, regulation, search warrant, subpoena, or court order.
conflicts.situation: Community Brands discloses a customer's Services Data to a third party to enforce its agreements, without the customer's permission and without a legal requirement.
conflicts.reason: The sharing section lets Community Brands disclose your data to enforce agreements or protect against harm. The Product and Services Data clause allows disclosure only with permission or legal compulsion, and no precedence is stated.

conflicts.permit: A parent who has already given Community Brands or our Customer permission to collect, use, and share their child’s personal information can, at any time, do the following
conflicts.prohibit: As such, Community Brands Websites are not directed at children under the age of 16 nor do we knowingly collect information from children under the age of 16.
conflicts.situation: A parent gives Community Brands permission to collect personal information from their 12-year-old child who uses a Community Brands Website or Service.
conflicts.reason: The children section says Community Brands does not knowingly collect information from children under 16. The parental access section assumes Community Brands collects children's data with parental permission, and neither section limits the other.

conflicts.permit: We may also allow certain third-party analytics service providers to include cookies and web beacons within the pages of the Websites on our behalf and to retain and use the information received from such cookies and web beacons themselves.
conflicts.prohibit: These third-party service providers are limited to only accessing or using this data to provide services to us and must provide reasonable assurances that they will appropriately safeguard the data.
conflicts.situation: Google Analytics collects visit data through cookies on a Community Brands Website and retains and uses that data for its own purposes.
conflicts.reason: The analytics clause lets providers retain and use the collected information themselves. The sharing section limits service providers to using website data only to serve Community Brands, and the policy does not reconcile the two.

conflicts.permit: These providers may collect and record information from our users’ devices, such as: bundle ID, language ID, operating system version ("OS"), device model, software developer kit ("SDK") version, unique device identifier (persistent / non-persistent), international mobile equipment identity (“IMEI”), Internet Protocol ("IP") address, and media access control ("MAC") address.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not share individual information with anyone else, except in cases of legal requirements.
conflicts.situation: A user plays an ad-supported AXgamesoft app, and the embedded Google, Unity, or Chartboost SDKs collect the device's IMEI, IP address, and advertising identifier.
conflicts.reason: The sharing section allows only legal disclosures and aggregate statistics. The third-party section lets ad and analytics providers in the apps collect device-level identifiers, and no exception for these providers is stated.

conflicts.permit: Such vendors may have access to certain Personally Identifiable Information on a need to know basis for evaluating Authorized Customers for service eligibility.
conflicts.prohibit: Personally Identifiable Information collected by 420nChill is securely stored and is not accessible to third parties or employees of 420nChill except for use as indicated above.
conflicts.situation: A partner vendor accesses an Authorized Customer's name and contact details to evaluate the customer's eligibility for a service.
conflicts.reason: The storage section bars third-party access except for uses indicated above. Vendor access for eligibility evaluation appears only later, and the earlier sections mention only payment vendors and other Authorized Customers.

conflicts.permit: these third parties SDK’s use your Cookies, unique device identifiers for advertising (Google Advertiser ID or IDFA) and Usage Data.
conflicts.prohibit: we decided to do not collect, store, disclose or transmit any kind of personal and non personal information
conflicts.situation: A user opens a Gora app that shows AdMob or StartApp ads, and the embedded SDKs read the advertising ID and usage data.
conflicts.reason: The policy states the company collects or transmits no personal or non-personal information. Its apps embed ad SDKs that use device advertising identifiers and usage data, and no exception for these SDKs is stated.
